data.findingId: 465bf2e:docs/runbooks/ci.md:59:Rollback misses the required status chec
data.title: Rollback misses the required status check on master
data.detail: The PM decided (card c-a5d4fd) to make ci a required check on master. Once set, disabling or deleting the workflow leaves every pull request waiting for a check that never comes, so GitHub blocks every merge, including the one that deletes the workflow. Fix: first rollback step removes ci from the required checks; correct the closing lines. PR #8 code review, finding 1.

data.findingId: 465bf2e:docs/runbooks/ci.md:46:The failing step is not the last one sho
data.title: The failing step is not the last one shown
data.detail: GitHub lists skipped steps and the Post Run and Complete job steps after the failure. Fix: say to find the step with the red X; later steps show as skipped. PR #8 code review, finding 2.

data.findingId: 465bf2e:docs/runbooks/ci.md:54:npm test builds the tools first, so buil
data.title: npm test builds the tools first, so build errors show in step 3
data.detail: scripts/run-tests.mjs line 32 builds the tools before tests, so an esbuild error fails npm test with no test name. Fix: add one sentence to the npm test bullet. PR #8 code review, finding 3.

data.findingId: 465bf2e:.github/workflows/ci.yml:11:No timeout-minutes on the ci job
data.title: No timeout-minutes on the ci job
data.detail: GitHub's default is 360 minutes. A hung test keeps ci pending for up to 6 hours and holds the sprint's merge chain. The first run took about 1 min 40 s. Fix: timeout-minutes: 15 on the job. PR #8 code review, finding 4.

data.findingId: 465bf2e:.github/workflows/ci.yml:15:Checkout leaves its token on disk
data.title: Checkout leaves its token on disk
data.detail: No step needs git credentials, so pull request code has no reason to see the token. Impact is small: the token can only read a public repository. Fix: persist-credentials: false on the checkout step. PR #8 code review, finding 5 (optional hardening).

data.findingId: f1222f2:docs/runbooks/ci.md:39:Runbook says tests never send notificati
data.title: Runbook says tests never send notifications; the requirement is never show
data.detail: DA-03.2 says running the tests never shows notifications to the PM. After da-t2 and da-t3 the notify suite sends to a stub notifier on purpose, so 'never send' becomes wrong. Fix: 'so tests never show a real notification.' PR #10 code review, L1. (L2, the feat(tests) commit type, has no file line; it is fixed by squash-merging with the PR title.)

data.findingId: f1222f2:docs/runbooks/ci.md:40:Runbook overstates TH-19: a suite with a
data.title: Runbook overstates TH-19: a suite with a fresh env does not get the switch
data.detail: 'so tests never send notifications' is stronger than TH-19's residual: a suite that builds a child's environment from scratch does not get the off switch. Fix: 'do not send real notifications. A suite that starts a child process must spread process.env into its env.' PR #10 security review, F3 (optional). Fixed together with code-review L1.

data.findingId: 932c730:tests/notify.test.ts:36:stubEnv accepts the real notifier path (
data.title: stubEnv accepts the real notifier path (TH-19)
data.detail: Security F1 and code review finding 3 (same defect). stubEnv checks only that the path is absolute, so stubEnv('/usr/bin/osascript') or stubEnv(notifierPath(process.env)) turns notifications on with platform darwin. A da-t4 to da-t9 test that does this shows a real banner on the PM's Mac or on the macos-latest CI runner, and the da-t4 rule ('dispatch only with notifierPath(stubEnv(...))') does not catch it. Fix: also throw unless the path is inside the suite's temporary folder (dirname(resolve(notifier)) === TMP), and add one throws line to the TH-19 test. STUB and <tmp>/missing still pass. Stricter than the TH-19 text; the architect would update threat-model.md:120-125 and design.md:408-411.

data.findingId: 932c730:tests/notify.test.ts:50:TH-19 test does not refuse a bare progra
data.title: TH-19 test does not refuse a bare program name (TH-3)
data.detail: Code review finding 2. The test refuses '' and 'relative/x' but not 'osascript', the one relative form that spawn looks up on PATH (TH-3). The code throws for it today; the test would not catch a later, weaker check. Fix: add throws(() => stubEnv('osascript'), /absolute path/).

data.findingId: 932c730:tests/notify.test.ts:44:The off-switch check does not stop the s
data.title: The off-switch check does not stop the suite (TH-19 residual)
data.detail: Security F3. DA-03.2 is an ordinary test; when it fails, runAll still runs every later test. From da-t4 on, a bundle run by hand or a runner change that drops the env would run later tests and CLI subprocesses with notifications on. Fix: before the temporary folder is made, exit 1 with a stderr line when process.env.PROJECT_COMPANION_NOTIFY !== 'off'; keep the named DA-03.2 test. The alternative is to keep it as the TH-19 residual already in threat-model.md:124-125.

data.findingId: 932c730:tests/notify.test.ts:45:DA-03.2 test cannot tell the runner's va
data.title: DA-03.2 test cannot tell the runner's value from the shell's
data.detail: Code review finding 1. The test reads process.env only. If the PM's shell exports PROJECT_COMPANION_NOTIFY=off and someone removes the env line in run-tests.mjs:58, a local npm test still passes. CI catches it because ci.yml does not set the variable. Matches the design's test seam; no change needed in this PR. Option: a devops task sets PROJECT_COMPANION_NOTIFY: on in the CI job so the test proves the runner overrides it.

data.findingId: 932c730:tests/notify.test.ts:39:A test can override the notifier after s
data.title: A test can override the notifier after spreading stubEnv (TH-19)
data.detail: Security F2. { ...stubEnv(STUB), PROJECT_COMPANION_NOTIFIER: '' } (or undefined, or a removed key) makes notifierPath fall back to /usr/bin/osascript with notifications on. An env built from nothing (for example { PATH }) loses the off switch. Fix: a review rule for da-t4 to da-t9, not code: every env in tests/notify.test.ts spreads process.env or stubEnv(...), nothing overrides PROJECT_COMPANION_NOTIFIER or PROJECT_COMPANION_NOTIFY after stubEnv, and every stubEnv path is inside the temporary folder. Check: grep -nE 'PROJECT_COMPANION_NOTIF|env: *\{|stubEnv\(' tests/notify.test.ts.

data.findingId: 932c730:tests/notify.test.ts:28:The stub's hold loop has no upper limit
data.title: The stub's hold loop has no upper limit
data.detail: Security F4. If a later detached DA-02.3 test is interrupted (Ctrl-C) before clean-up, the detached stub keeps polling the hold file with sleep 0.05 until someone kills it. In this PR the only held run is bounded by the 5 s spawnSync timeout and the finally. Fix: bound the loop, for example i=0; while [ -e "$STUB_HOLD" ] && [ "$i" -lt 600 ]; do ...; i=$((i+1)); done.

data.reason: 3 of 10 sprint tasks merged before the sprint starts; no decision overdue
data.body:
Bottom line: Decision alerts are on track. 3 of the 10 tasks in sprint 2026-w42 are merged before the sprint starts on Monday, and the 4th (the notification record) is in review.

Done this week:
- CI now runs on every pull request: npm ci, typecheck, the tests and build:tools (PR 8).
- A test run can never show you a notification. The test runner sets the off switch (PR 10). The notify test suite uses only a stand-in notifier, and it stops at once if the off switch is missing (PR 11).
- The notification record is built: one git-ignored line for each notified decision, written so that no planted link can send it outside the project. It is in review as PR 12.
- devolps is at 0.3.12. You can now delegate one sprint's merges and questions with /devolps:delegate. You did this for sprint 2026-w42, until 16 October.

Next week:
- Finish sprint 2026-w42: the notifier, the off switch and macOS check, failure messages, the alert from gate request and card open, and the proofs that a broken notifier never changes a command (tasks da-t4 to da-t9).
- When the last task merges, prepare the release and ask you for the release gate.

Risks:
- A real notification on your Mac during development — unlikely, and serious if it happens (test text on your screen). The off switch, the suite's stop, and a review rule on every notify test guard it. Owner: EM, checked at each review.
- A tracker-log merge conflict after each squash merge — certain to come back, low impact. Under your delegation the EM merges with git merge -X theirs and checks that no log line is lost, and stops if the check fails. Owner: EM.
- Two track cards still show as open although you confirmed the tracks (known bug ee2e49d6) — certain, low impact. Planned for sprint 2026-w43. Owner: EM.

Decisions needed from you:
- Publish this update — type /devolps:publish-update <week>, or tell me what to change — by Monday 12 October.
- Confirm the Bugfix track for the 3 proposed bugs (15753492, ee2e49d6, d5ebde85) — options: Bugfix as proposed, or another track — recommendation: Bugfix — by the sprint 2026-w43 planning.

data.findingId: ffaa857:lib/project/notify-record.ts:65:No test makes the .gitignore write fail
data.title: No test makes the .gitignore write fail with an error other than EEXIST (TH-13)
data.detail: Code review. Two wrong versions pass every test: line 65 ignoring every .gitignore error and appending anyway (TH-13 says nothing is appended), or line 64 deleted so the reason names the folder, not <folder>/.gitignore (design 3.3 reason table). Fix: a test, skipped as root, that makes .project-notify/ a real folder with an empty record.jsonl, sets the folder to 0o500, expects RecordError 'EACCES <root>/.project-notify/.gitignore' and record.jsonl still empty, and restores 0o700 in a finally. Blocks the merge until fixed. Security note N4 is the same gap.

data.findingId: ffaa857:lib/project/notify-record.ts:68:Opening a FIFO at record.jsonl blocks fo
data.title: Opening a FIFO at record.jsonl blocks for ever (TH-8, D3)
data.detail: Security F1. openSync(record, O_WRONLY|...) waits for a reader if record.jsonl is a named pipe; try/catch cannot catch a wait. After da-t7 every gate request and card open would hang. Git cannot store a FIFO, so it needs a tar archive or a local process. Very low likelihood. EM decision (questions delegated): fix now, the safe option: add O_NONBLOCK (no reader gives ENXIO) and refuse a non-regular file after fstat. N1 (O_NOFOLLOW does not refuse a hard link) is recorded, not fixed: git cannot plant one.

data.findingId: ffaa857:lib/project/notify-record.ts:84:readRecord follows symlinks and has none
data.title: readRecord follows symlinks and has none of appendRecord's checks (TH-21, read side)
data.detail: Security F2. readFileSync follows a symlinked folder or record. Today only tests call readRecord. A later metric command could read a planted link (an outside JSONL file, a FIFO, a huge file). EM decision: no code change now; rule for any non-test caller: harden readRecord first (lstat the folder, O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK, require isFile) and the architect adds a D3 read flow to the threat model.

data.findingId: ffaa857:lib/project/notify-record.ts:65:An existing .gitignore, folder mode or t
data.title: An existing .gitignore, folder mode or tracked record is trusted as is (TH-13 residual)
data.detail: Security F3. Any existing .gitignore counts (type and content unchecked); modes 0o700/0o600 hold only for entries this code creates; a record git already tracks is not ignored. In other projects without the root /.project-notify/ rule, a cloned repo could commit .project-notify/.gitignore as a symlink or empty file, and git add -A would then commit the record. Impact small: titles and commands are already in the committed event log (TH-6). Matches design step 2. Not fixed. Accepting it as a TH-13 residual is the PM's call (design level), recorded for the PM.

data.findingId: 2861b2d:lib/project/notify-record.ts:45:The suite does not prove O_NONBLOCK on i
data.title: The suite does not prove O_NONBLOCK on its own
data.detail: Backend-engineer hand-off, PR #12 rework. Removing only O_NONBLOCK from OPEN_FLAGS still passes 14/14: the FIFO test opens a reader first (so it can never hang) and therefore proves the isFile check, not the flag. A scratch probe in a child process shows the open then waits (killed after 5 s). EM decision (questions delegated): keep it; the flag is checked by reading. A child-process test with a kill timeout that expects ENXIO can come later if wanted.

data.findingId: 2861b2d:tests/notify.test.ts:132:A skipped test prints ok (root, or no mk
data.title: A skipped test prints ok (root, or no mkfifo)
data.detail: Backend-engineer hand-off. tests/harness.ts has no skip state, so the root-only TH-13 EACCES test and the mkfifo-only TH-8 test return early and print ok. On this Mac and the macos-latest CI runner they run (uid 501, /usr/bin/mkfifo present). EM decision: keep; a harness skip result is a separate change to tests/harness.ts, outside this task.

data.findingId: 25652b9:lib/project/notify.ts:55:dispatch accepts a program path that is
data.title: dispatch accepts a program path that is not absolute (TH-3)
data.detail: Security F1 and code review L1 (same defect). For a bare name, accessSync checks the current folder while spawn searches PATH, so the checked file and the program that runs can differ; under npx, node_modules/.bin comes first. The module header claims TH-3 for the whole module. EM decision (questions delegated): fix in this PR, the safe option: the first line of dispatch throws DispatchError('path', null) for a path that is not absolute; test with a name that is not on PATH (pc-no-such-notifier), recorded as the one exception to the stubEnv rule for dispatch calls.

data.findingId: 25652b9:tests/notify.test.ts:287:A STUB_OUT or STUB_HOLD already set in t
data.title: A STUB_OUT or STUB_HOLD already set in the shell leaks into the suite (TH-19 hygiene)
data.detail: Security F2. The last dispatch test starts the stub with the inherited environment and assumes STUB_OUT is not set. With STUB_OUT set in the developer's shell, the stub writes the hostile text (inert) into that outside folder; with STUB_HOLD naming an existing file, a detached sh polls for up to 600 rounds after the suite ends. EM decision: fix in this PR: stop the suite at the top when STUB_OUT or STUB_HOLD is set, next to the off-switch guard.

data.findingId: 25652b9:tests/notify.test.ts:285:No test here proves that dispatch never
data.title: No test here proves that dispatch never waits
data.detail: Code review L2. The stub inherits process.env (no STUB_OUT), so it exits at once; removing detached, stdio 'ignore' or unref fails neither dispatch test. The PR body claimed 'never waits'. EM decision: reword the PR body; the no-wait proof is DA-02.3 in da-t8 (6042a875). By reading, lines 63-69 match design 3.3 exactly.
